## TL;DR

Task #1077 closes the check-window drift gaps called out when #1061 landed. The core classifier and filesystem tripwire were already implemented on `main` during #1061 review rounds (history walk in `checkGateHeadDriftAllowed`, fail-closed net deltas, and `trackedSourceSnapshot` around task self-checks). This session adds production-path regression tests for transient source commits that leave a net-zero tree, and confirms handoff and direct task `repoos check` both refuse a green result when that happens.

## Work and rationale

The original #1061 drift check compared only the endpoint tree between check start and check end. A source commit followed by a revert inside the same window left an empty net diff, so validation could report success after observing intermediate source. Review round 12 of #1061 fixed the classifier to walk first-parent commits in the gate window, classify merges against the checked tree, and fail closed when unexplained net source paths remain. Round 13–14 added working-tree snapshots so direct file writes are detected when commits do not move `HEAD`.

Task #1077 was filed to track that follow-up explicitly. When work started, the feature branch matched `main` on source files: the fix was already live. Remaining acceptance work was criterion 4 — tests through real call sites, not only the unit helper — and documentation already updated in `docs/check-run-history.md` and `user-docs/check.md`.

I merged current `main` into the task branch (fast-forward), then added two tests. The handoff test reuses the established fake-`repoos` fixture: during the gate the stand-in check script adds `late.txt`, commits, removes it, and commits again. Handoff must fail at the drift step with both commit subjects and the path, even though `late.txt` is absent from the final tree. The self-check test extends `check-remote-wip.test.ts`: the noop plan step runs the same commit-and-revert sequence on `src/app.ts` while the task worktree holds a check-gate lock, asserting a `worktree-drift` failure and proving the endpoint blob matches check start.

Close-out validation was not given a third duplicate test. Its merge-gate runs the same `repoos check` child with the same drift step in the task worktree; the new self-check test exercises that code path directly.

## Approaches tried

The first handoff test attempted to rewrite `source.txt` during the fake check, restoring the same bytes the handoff commit had just landed. Handoff completed successfully: the scenario did not match how the production handoff path snapshots and commits the implement tree before the gate. Switching to the add-file-then-remove pattern (analogous to the existing “late commit” test, but with a net-zero endpoint) matched production behavior and failed as required.

No classifier changes were needed in this branch; effort focused on proving the existing production wiring rather than re-implementing #1061 work.

## Challenges and blockers

None blocking. The branch began with zero source delta versus `main`; scope was test coverage and verification, not new drift logic.

## Key learnings

A net-zero tree diff is necessary but not sufficient for check-window integrity: the commit sequence during the gate must be inspected. Handoff integration tests need scenarios that respect the commit-before-gate ordering; mutating files the handoff is about to commit produces misleading greens. When a follow-up task is filed against code that already landed via another task’s review rounds, the first step is to diff against `main` and read recent engineering reports before rewriting logic.
